elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Inserted paragraph: "TrueLink shall defend and indemnify Client and its affiliates against any third-party claim..." — express defence duty running to Client and its affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Same inserted sentence indemnifies "Client and its affiliates against any third-party claim" under limbs (i)-(iv).

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Limb (i): claims "alleging that the Interface, any related software, the Hosting Services or the Support Services infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right" — covers the service/deliverable set actually supplied under this Agreement.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Limb (ii): claims "arising out of TrueLink's breach of applicable law".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Limb (iii) is confined to "unauthorized access to or disclosure of Client Content or Credit Data caused by TrueLink". "Credit Data" is defined in §1(d) only as raw repository credit data that is at least 31 days old/archived AND "not combined, compared with or against, integrated or presented in any way with any Client Proprietary Information"; fresh borrower credit data and data combined with Client Proprietary Information therefore fall outside the trigger, and Client Content does not fill the gap. The trigger covers selected named data types rather than all data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Client.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Limb (iv): claims "arising out of TrueLink's gross negligence or willful misconduct".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: "Client shall give TrueLink prompt written notice of any claim indemnified under this Section 12".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: "TrueLink shall have control of the defense and settlement of the claim".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: "Client shall provide reasonable cooperation in the defense".

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Section 12(a) as rendered now has only two limbs: "(i) any claim arising out of or relating to Client Content ... and (ii) any breach by Client of any applicable state or federal law, rule or regulation"; the breach-of-Agreement, System/Credit Repository default, Web Site and product/service-injury triggers are removed.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Inserted limb (i) covers third-party claims alleging the Interface, related software, Hosting Services or Support Services infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no Customer-modification exclusion is inserted, which is more favourable to Client than the permitted carve-out; the condition does not apply.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no combination exclusion inserted; absence is more favourable to Client, so the permission is not engaged.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no Client-specification exclusion inserted; absence is more favourable to Client, so the permission is not engaged.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: No procure/modify/replace remedy appears anywhere in the rendered Section 12 or the inserted paragraph.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund obligation is inserted; the rendered text contains no fee-refund mechanic tied to unavailable IP remedies.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No 3x annual fees super-cap is added; the retained Section 12 cap language is expressly left untouched and does not create an indemnity super-cap.

reasons: Preferred level is incomplete on one element only: the data-breach limb. Repair limb (iii) in operative language so it is not keyed to the two narrow defined categories — e.g. "any unauthorized access to, use or disclosure of Client Content, Credit Data or any other data of Client, its affiliates or their respective customers that is provided to, transmitted through or processed by TrueLink". As drafted, §1(d) excludes credit data less than 31 days old/not yet archived and any data combined with Client Proprietary Information, so the most sensitive live borrower data is outside the indemnity trigger.

Fallback level is not an alternative route here: the proposal adds no procure/modify/replace remedy, no refund of applicable fees where those remedies are unavailable, and no 3x annual fees super-cap, so three fallback elements fail.

Minimality holds: op 1 removes only the Client-indemnity triggers outside "Client Content" and "Client's breach of law" (including the "Web Site or" trigger and the product/service-injury limb), and op 2 adds only the four indemnity limbs plus the notice/control/cooperation procedure required by the checklist — no survival tail, expense language, extra damages categories or boilerplate.

Intent is preserved: existing §12(b) TrueLink breach indemnity and the §12 cap (Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11) survive without contradiction; "Client Content" (§1(b)) and "Credit Data" (§1(d)) are defined, and the new procedure sentence's reference to "this Section 12" is internally consistent. Confirm "Hosting Services", "Support Services" and "Interface" are the defined service terms used elsewhere so limb (i) leaves no dangling reference.

Deterministic gates report element coverage as satisfied, but on substance the coverage gate over-reads limb (iii): naming Client Content and the narrowly defined Credit Data is not coverage of a Vendor-caused data breach generally.
